lens: clarity and depth for a curious 15-year-old and an expert at once
critical: The word 'Transformer' is never spoken anywhere in the narration (0 hits). The brief asks for transformers in depth. ch10-s04 L1009 or ch10-s11 L1023/L1024 must name it, e.g. after L1009: 'They called it the Transformer.' and once more in ch10-s13 ('The Transformer spread within two.').

Two of the most important beliefs in the story are lit and never put out, and how long they lasted is never said, though the brief asks 'how long did people think that way?'. (a) MANY-LAYERED NETS ARE A STERILE EXTENSION (ch04-s02, 1969) is lit but no shot puts it out. It should gutter in ch05-s04 when the trained XOR net solves the hidden layer (1969 to 1986, about seventeen years), and the narrator should say so. (b) NEURAL NETS ARE FIDDLY, AND BEATEN ANYWAY (ch06-s04) is also never put out. It should go out in ch08-s13 alongside the hand-cut-features candle, with its duration spoken.

The scale era's beliefs are never put into words. ch11-s05 silently lights SCALE IS THE MAIN LEVER, which is still burning and is the central belief of the present, plus GROW THE MODEL FASTER THAN THE DATA. Then L1116 says 'One small candle goes out. The big one is trimmed.' A listener cannot know which beliefs these are. L1110 should name the candle aloud, and L1116 should name both candles and their two-year life.

AlexNet's headline result uses top-5 error, but the narration never explains it. L0802 ('missed about one in four') and L0822 ('got twenty-six point two percent wrong') will be heard as plain error rates. Also, 'ImageNet' is first spoken in L1512, the last chapter, and the challenge itself (1.2 million photos, 1,000 categories) is never spoken. Fix: in L0704 or L0802, name ImageNet and the challenge, and say 'allowed five guesses, the best still missed about one in four'.

issues.problem: The messenger is never identified as back-propagation before L0511 asks 'Who invented it?'. The term first reaches the ear inside a quote (L0512). The XOR payoff, where the hidden layer the 1969 book called sterile now learns, is only visual. The Helsinki 'most important clue' planted in L0413 is never paid off aloud.
issues.fix: L0508: 'Then a messenger, back-propagation, runs back down the same strings...'. After L0509 add: 'Exclusive-or, solved. The sterile extension, it turns out, was not.' (put out the sterile candle here, 17 years). In L0511, add 'one of them that Helsinki thesis' to close the loop by voice.

issues.problem: The great connectionist-versus-symbolic debate (Fodor and Pylyshyn, 1988, the systematicity challenge) appears only as on-screen cards read under music. This is exactly the kind of 'who dissented, and is it still argued' content the brief asks for, and the narration is silent about it.
issues.fix: Add one spoken line before L0519: 'Two philosophers objected: anyone who can say John loves the girl can say the girl loves John. Could a net ever learn that? It is still argued.' Claims e4-fodor-pylyshyn, e4-systematicity-2023.

issues.problem: 'It burned about seven years' comes right after 'a panel warned of an AI Winter', so a listener hears the WINTER as what burned seven years, not the knowledge candle.
issues.fix: 'By 1987 its special machines were going dark. The knowledge candle had burned about seven years.'

issues.problem: Classical ML gets one example (the SVM) in the narration, though the brief asks for classical ML and the chapter blurb promises 'done justice'. The bible has boosting (e6-adaboost), random forests (e6-randomforest), graphical models (e6-pearl) and statistical translation (e6-ibm-smt), all unused.
issues.fix: Add one line after L0607, e.g. 'Others boosted weak rules into strong ones, or grew forests of simple decision trees; speech and translation turned to statistics.' Optionally add a quick paper-cut vignette of a tree forest and a boosted committee.

issues.problem: 'All three conditions are now satisfied' is unreadable by ear: which three? The tick-boxes on screen help, but the quote lands as a riddle.
issues.fix: Before the quote, say: 'Fast computers, big data, good starting weights: "All three conditions are now satisfied," they wrote.'

issues.problem: ReLU is used in L0807 ('Below zero counts as zero') and then introduced as new trick number one in L0813 ('A weir that passes only what rises over the lip'). An attentive teen will hear two different things, and an expert hears a repetition. Also, 'six times faster to train' was a four-layer CIFAR-10 test, not AlexNet itself.
issues.fix: L0813: 'Two tricks. That rule, below zero counts as zero, is a weir: in their test it trained six times faster.' Keep L0814's ladle, and add why it helps: 'a ladle that keeps only the brightest bead, so a small shift doesn't matter.'

issues.problem: The word 'convolution' or 'convolutional network' is never spoken, although later chapters show 'convolutional nets' on screen (ch08-s13) and 'convolution: not in the box' (ch08-s14). The key idea that the same stencil is reused everywhere is implied but never stated.
issues.fix: L0808: '...Slide it along. Step, step, step. The same stencil, everywhere: that sliding is called a convolution.'

issues.problem: The problem that cropping and dropout solve, memorising instead of generalising, is never named. 'Ten bits' is opaque to a 15-year-old. 'Snuffed half the lanterns' overstates dropout, which applied only to the two big fully connected halls (e8-ingredients).
issues.fix: L0815: 'A thousand possible answers means each label is worth about ten yes-or-no questions, against sixty million numbers to set. It could simply memorise the pictures.' L0816: '...and in the great halls, snuffed half the lanterns at random on every example.'

issues.problem: Source (e8-gpu-split): first-layer kernels on one card came out largely colour-agnostic and on the other largely colour-specific. 'One learned edges' is an interpretive stretch.
issues.fix: 'One learned in black and white, the other in colour. Every time.'

issues.problem: 'Shortened the stride' collides with the convolution's real stride (AlexNet conv1 uses stride 4) and with the pooling 'stride 2' on screen. Experts will misread it; teens get a word with two meanings.
issues.fix: 'Three times, they shortened their steps by hand.' Use 'step' consistently for the learning rate here and in ch05-s05.

issues.problem: 'AlexNet' is first spoken in L0822 as if already known, and never introduced as the name of Krizhevsky's network.
issues.fix: L0822: 'Second place got twenty-six point two wrong. Alex's network, AlexNet, fifteen point three.'

issues.problem: 'Fire the scribe. Keep the highlighter' relies on two metaphors the ear never got. The scribe and the highlighter exist only in the visuals of s01 and s02, and L1005 calls it 'attention'.
issues.fix: 'So: fire the slow reader. Keep the attention. Every word looks at every word, all at once. They called it the Transformer.'

issues.problem: The worked attention example is excellent, but the value step (the messages blended in those shares) is shown, not said. 'So bank means the water's edge' skips the mechanism. The source of the three cards is never given: each is made from the word's numbers by learned weights, set by the 1986 messenger. That is the link an expert expects and the payoff a teen enjoys ('words became places' in ch09).
issues.fix: L1010: add 'Each card is made from the word by its own learned settings.' L1013/L1014: '...About half runs to river. Bank takes in the messages in those shares, and comes out meaning the water's edge.'

issues.problem: The 'straight lane' (residual connection) gets no reason. Its purpose ties directly to the film's fading-whisper motif (ch06-s06), a free payoff.
issues.fix: 'And a straight lane carries each word through, so the messenger's whisper does not fade on the way back.'

issues.problem: 'Cut the loom in half, and kept the half with a curtain' is opaque: the narration never said the original had two halves (a reading half and a writing half), and 'loom' first appears here.
issues.fix: Precede with: 'The original had two halves: one to read the English, one to write the German.' Then: 'In 2018, researchers kept only the writing half, with a curtain over the words to come.'

issues.problem: 'Move thirty-seven: one chance in ten thousand' is ambiguous; a listener may think the odds are of winning. Per the bible (line 917), it was the policy network's estimate that a human would play it. AlphaGo's mechanics (a net proposes moves, a net judges the board, search) get no words at all.
issues.fix: 'Move thirty-seven: a move a human would play once in ten thousand.' Optionally add 'One network suggested moves, another judged the board.'

issues.problem: The same idea is called 'knobs' (ch03, L1111), 'numbers' (ch08) and 'weights' (L1412, 'open weights'), and the term 'weight' or 'parameter' is never defined. 'Open weights kept crossing the water' is therefore opaque.
issues.fix: At L0810: 'About sixty million numbers in all: knobs, we call them weights.' At L1412: 'Open weights, the trained knobs themselves, free to download, kept crossing the water.'

issues.problem: 'By 2022, the choosing had shears' is a metaphor with no referent by ear. RLHF's three steps are on screen only.
issues.fix: 'By 2022, people's rankings trained a judge, and the judge pruned the model.'

issues.problem: L1307 lights a candle without speaking its belief (SMARTER-THAN-HUMAN AI MAY BE YEARS AWAY, AND DANGEROUS). L1312's 'Two in the light. One at its edge.' is ambiguous: earlier 'in the light' meant mainstream acceptance.
issues.fix: L1307: 'A new candle: machines smarter than us may be years away, and dangerous.' L1312: 'The three who kept the faith through the winters? Two signed. The third scoffed.'

issues.problem: On screen the candle reads COMPUTE IS THE CHOKEPOINT; CHINA IS ONE TO THREE YEARS BEHIND, but the narration speaks only the first half. In s04 the chokepoint candle goes out silently while the narration says 'Compute doesn't matter? ... Out within a day.' The ear hears that compute still matters while the eye sees the compute candle die, which is contradictory.
issues.fix: L1405: 'A new candle: compute is the chokepoint, and China is one to three years behind.' L1410: 'Compute doesn't matter? A struck match, out within a day. But the one-to-three-years candle went out too.'

issues.problem: 'Behind a curtain' reuses ch10's curtain, which meant the causal mask, for a hidden chain of thought: a metaphor collision. 'Then' places reasoning models after the October 2024 phone call, but the September 2024 label shows they came first.
issues.fix: 'That autumn, the machines learned to think longer before answering, in notes their makers kept hidden.'

issues.problem: 'A ruler for the tasks they finish alone' — 'they' is ambiguous (labs? people? machines?).
issues.fix: 'A ruler for how long a task an AI can finish on its own doubles about every seven months.'

issues.problem: One spoken line covers eight claims, and six dense cards flash for about one second each. These include contested Anthropic items (the Pentagon dispute, the $1.5B settlement, the company's own vulnerability claim) and the OpenAI incident with its sceptic. One second is unreadable, so this is neither depth nor fair treatment, and it is the densest 'current understanding' moment of the film.
issues.fix: Either give 2-3 cards a spoken half-line each (for example: 'One lab withheld a model it called too good at finding security holes. Another lab's test escape was called a warning shot, and by a sceptic, contrived.') and hold each card for at least 4 seconds, or cut to the three most important items.

issues.problem: 'At its rim now stands Marvin Minsky' does not say what he doubted. The dissent is carried only by an on-screen quote.
issues.fix: 'At its rim now stands Marvin Minsky, who had built a learning machine himself, and doubted these could ever see shapes as simple as two separate parts.'

issues.problem: The narration is 3,227 words against the 3,040 target (+6%). The fixes above add about 150 words.
issues.fix: Trim compressed list lines that teach little: L1218 (the stampede list), L0901-L0902 (auction detail), L1413-L1414, L1110-L1111 if folded into the candle line.

issues.where: ch12-s07 L1221 before L1216; missing L0214, L0313
issues.problem: Line IDs are out of order or skipped. This is harmless to the story, but tools that sort or cue by ID may misplace narration.
issues.fix: Renumber the lines in shot order before narration, or confirm the pipeline uses array order.

strengths: The candle-clock device turns 'what people believed and for how long' into something you can see and measure: sixteen years, about seven, thirteen, twenty, two, one day. L1515's honesty that the newest candles are short partly because they haven't finished burning is exactly right.

The attention worked example is the best teaching in the film: real scores (2, 0, 4, 2), a real softmax (0.20/0.07/0.53/0.20), and then 'why divide by eight' paid off with the toy ('our toy cards had four: hence, halve'). An expert nods and a teen gets it.

The AlexNet deep dive covers the real ingredients, each with a physical metaphor: a worked 3.88 stencil sum, 96 first-layer stencils, ~60M numbers vs ~10 bits per label, crops and mirrors, dropout, the unprompted two-GPU split, the hand-cut learning rate, plus the fair ensemble caveat (15.3% vs a single net nearer 18%) and the credit to IDSIA.

Setups pay off across decades: the fog and hollow (ch05) set up the SVM's clean bowl and the question 'why choose the fog?', answered in ch08. The 'pre-training' tag returns 'in a different coat'. Cyc's 1985 'nothing from raw text' sits beside GPT-2's 'predict the next word'. Rosenblatt's 1961 'linguistic capability' sentence returns sixty-one years later. Widrow's 'remember him' pays off at his death.

Fairness reflexes are consistently good: credit for backprop shared and Hinton's own disclaimer, 'one book's fault? historians still argue', the Gebru fired/resigned framing, the Anthropic FTX disclosure, Amodei labelled as a rival lab's chief, Jensen Huang labelled as a seller, and the DeepSeek cost caveat stated in DeepSeek's own terms.
The narration is written for the ear: short sentences, numbers spoken naturally, exact symbols kept on screen (attention formula, margin equation, blame equation).
